title: Effects of background color on growth performance and developmental stability in juvenile Amphiprion ocellaris
content:
Abstract

Tank background color is an easily modifiable environmental factor in aquaculture; however, its effects on the developmental stability of coral reef fish remain poorly understood. This study investigated the influence of six background colors (black, green, red, white, yellow, and transparent) on the growth performance, survival, and developmental stability of juvenile clownfish (Amphiprion ocellaris). Juvenile fish (30 days old) were reared for 56 days under controlled conditions (25 ± 0.5°C, salinity 34 ± 1‰, 12 L:12D photoperiod). Survival, weight gain, specific growth rate (SGR), and fluctuating asymmetry (FA) across six morphological traits were assessed. Red and yellow backgrounds significantly enhanced survival (>82%). Yellow background resulted in the highest weight gain (142.86%) and SGR (1.58% day−1), while black background produced the lowest growth. White background induced the highest FA values, particularly in head length and pelvic fin distance, indicating developmental instability. In contrast, yellow background consistently yielded the lowest FA. Multivariate analyses (PERMANOVA, R 2 = 0.0386, p = 0.0025; LDA cross-validation accuracy = 23%) showed that although background color had a statistically significant effect on overall FA, it explained only a small fraction of total variance (<4%). Variance decomposition revealed that individual-level random variation dominated (>95% of total variance). These results demonstrate that background color significantly affects both growth and developmental stability in A. ocellaris, with yellow being the optimal choice for rearing. The practical effect on developmental stability is modest compared to intrinsic individual variability, but yellow tanks are recommended for clownfish aquaculture to improve productivity and welfare.
